title: BPP Languages in the Second Existential Level
statement: Let $E$ be a verifier model closed under polynomial majority amplification and under the verifier that accepts when at least one of polynomially many runs accepts after its random bits are combined by bitwise exclusive-or with a second witness. If $L$ has an efficient randomized verifier accepting members and rejecting nonmembers with probability at least $2/3$, then there is an efficient two-witness verifier $N$ and polynomial bounds $p_1(n)=a_1(n+1)^{k_1}$ and $p_2(n)=a_2(n+1)^{k_2}$ such that, for every Boolean word $x$, membership in $L$ is equivalent to the existence of a Boolean word $u$ of length $p_1(|x|)$ for which every Boolean word $v$ of length $p_2(|x|)$ satisfies $N(x,u,v)=\mathrm{true}$.
hypotheses_covered: $E$ is closed under polynomial majority amplification
$E$ is closed under the polynomial shift-and-or verifier construction
$L$ has an efficient randomized verifier with member acceptance and nonmember rejection probabilities at least $2/3$
